trigger: Security noticed an unfamiliar app reading patient records through the EMR's FHIR API, launched by cardiology users at H17.

why: The symptom describes an unfamiliar app accessing patient records through SMART on FHIR, so I’m checking estate-wide unregistered-app findings.
The finding names cardiorisk.example.com; I’m tracing its access path from the initiating group through users and APIs to patient data.
The observed app path reaches the FHIR API and EMR database; I’m identifying the teams that own and actually resolve these components.
Before treating this as a new security issue, I’m checking prior investigation memory for confirmed or rejected facts about the app and its data path.
The open critical D14 finding and observed access path show an unregistered app reading EMR patient data; opening a critical incident for the team responsible for the FHIR API.

args.short_description: Unregistered app accessing patient records through EMR FHIR API from H17 cardiology users

reasons: An open critical D14 finding identifies cardiorisk.example.com as an unregistered SMART on FHIR app reading EMR data via the FHIR API.
Netflow observed 19 users in grp-H17-CARD-physician launching the app over 8 days, with 18928 API calls and emr-db-01 as data.
The app has no CMDB record, and the observed path reaches patient records.

warn.why: Act on the unregistered app's access through the FHIR API.
The observed app path reaches this data component.

actions: Opened a priority 1 - Critical incident ticket for cardiorisk.example.com assigned to NW-EMR-Apps.
Recommend investigating the app and its access to patient records.
